purpose: Use already-admitted propagation, buffering and branching cases to reject single-factor explanations and rank measurements that distinguish the remaining plant-side propagation filters.

cases.observed_chain: hidden S-morph stigma access failure -> S-to-L pollen transfer -> much lower open fruit set in S than L

autonomous_reproductive_assurance.evidence: Published hand-pollination context reports self fruit set 0% in both morphs, intramorph S-to-S 5.9% and L-to-L 0%, while intermorph hand fruit set is 82.4% and 82.6%.
autonomous_reproductive_assurance.interpretation: Low autonomous/intramorph reproductive escape is consistent with an access bottleneck reaching reproduction, but controlled all-pollinator dependency is not measured.

physical_access_or_functional_matching.evidence: The source reports that dominant Apis cannot reach the hidden S-morph stigma and pollen transfer is unidirectional S-to-L.
physical_access_or_functional_matching.interpretation: This is the clearest current physical-access propagation case, but it is categorical rather than a numeric signed-position measurement.

partner_effectiveness_or_service_redunda.evidence: Directional pollen transfer shows morph-specific service failure; standardized single-visit pollen deposition is unavailable.
partner_effectiveness_or_service_redunda.interpretation: Service is asymmetric enough to support the propagation chain, but no common effectiveness scale exists.

resource_compensation.interpretation: No source-locked resource-compensation mechanism is available.

colonization_or_establishment_filtering.interpretation: The focal plant is endemic; the relevant contemporary contrast concerns pollinator replacement/access, not introduction of the plant lineage.

network_rewiring_or_context.interpretation: Current visitor composition is documented, while historical replacement is inferred rather than experimentally reconstructed.

direct_reproductive_dependency.interpretation: Open fruit asymmetry is not an all-pollinator exclusion dependency estimate.

cases.observed_chain: source-native signed bill-flower mismatch -> pollen-contact/nectar-robbing differences -> damage alters nectar replenishment, but fruit and seed performance remain high

autonomous_reproductive_assurance.interpretation: Controlled reproductive dependency/autonomous assurance is not available for the matched 2026 lobelioid bridge.

physical_access_or_functional_matching.evidence: The source-native bill-minus-flower axis predicts interaction quality, yet the closely overlapping experimental study retains high reproductive performance.
physical_access_or_functional_matching.interpretation: Functional mismatch can affect interaction quality without fixing the final reproductive sign.

partner_effectiveness_or_service_redunda.evidence: Fertile-structure contact occurs in 43% of visits and nectar robbing in 39%; fruit/seed performance remains high.
partner_effectiveness_or_service_redunda.interpretation: Interaction quality alone is insufficient to identify reproductive collapse.

resource_compensation.evidence: Experimental floral damage changes nectar replenishment while reproductive performance remains high.
resource_compensation.interpretation: Resource replenishment/compensation is a live buffering candidate, but the experiment does not identify it as the unique cause of reproductive resilience.

colonization_or_establishment_filtering.interpretation: The focal lobelioids are native; the current bridge concerns persistence after bird losses rather than introduced-plant establishment.

network_rewiring_or_context.interpretation: Historical versus contemporary nectar-feeding bird assemblages differ, so partner turnover is part of the upstream change.

direct_reproductive_dependency.interpretation: This is the highest-value missing discriminator for distinguishing low dependency from post-interaction compensation.

cases.observed_chain: greater island autonomous selfing capacity and longer corollas coexist with no detected current island reduction in visitation/pollen transfer or general island pollen limitation

autonomous_reproductive_assurance.evidence: Island populations have higher autonomous self-pollination capacity, strongest on recently colonized Santa Cruz Island.
autonomous_reproductive_assurance.interpretation: Reproductive assurance is a strong system-specific candidate, but it cannot be treated as a response to a current service deficit that was not detected.

physical_access_or_functional_matching.evidence: Per-visit effectiveness differed among hummingbird species but was not associated with corolla length.
physical_access_or_functional_matching.interpretation: Current floral matching does not explain the observed island corolla difference in the locked source summary.

partner_effectiveness_or_service_redunda.evidence: Visitation and pollen transfer were not lower on islands and island fruit set was not generally pollen limited.
partner_effectiveness_or_service_redunda.interpretation: This is an alternative-mechanism case rather than a clean test of buffering after measured service loss.

resource_compensation.interpretation: No source-locked resource-compensation mechanism is required by the current evidence.

colonization_or_establishment_filtering.evidence: The plant is introduced and the strongest autonomous-selfing capacity occurs on a recently colonized island population.
colonization_or_establishment_filtering.interpretation: Colonization/establishment filtering remains a live explanation for the island trait/reproductive pattern.

network_rewiring_or_context.interpretation: Pollinator composition differs, but current aggregate service is not lower on islands.

direct_reproductive_dependency.interpretation: Autogamy, emasculation and pollen-limitation experiments provide substantial reproductive-assurance/dependency information, but cross-paper/site-year linkage is incomplete.

cases.observed_chain: very large visitor-assemblage and visitation contrast -> similar self/outcross breeding-system index and negligible autogamy

autonomous_reproductive_assurance.evidence: Autogamy produced only three mature fruits in Guánica and two on Mona; the source concludes a pollen vector is required for effective reproduction.
autonomous_reproductive_assurance.interpretation: Stable breeding-system index across populations cannot be explained by high autonomous reproduction, so assurance is not a universal buffering mechanism.

physical_access_or_functional_matching.interpretation: No compatible quantitative trait-matching/access axis is recovered.

partner_effectiveness_or_service_redunda.evidence: Guánica is overwhelmingly Apis-dominated with about twice the source-reported visitation rate, whereas Mona has a richer/more even assemblage.
partner_effectiveness_or_service_redunda.interpretation: Compensatory abundance or functional redundancy is plausible but cannot be identified without direct effectiveness.

resource_compensation.interpretation: No source-locked plant resource-compensation mechanism is measured.

colonization_or_establishment_filtering.interpretation: The current source comparison is between populations of the same species and does not identify an establishment filter.

network_rewiring_or_context.interpretation: The visitor assemblages differ sharply in richness, dominance and visitation rate.

direct_reproductive_dependency.evidence: Self/outcross seed-set ISI is 0.60 versus 0.63 with P=0.77, but numeric open/outcross total-dependency ratios are not recovered.
direct_reproductive_dependency.interpretation: The plant-side breeding state appears similar across the strong exposure contrast, but the exact dependency estimand remains missing.

cases.observed_chain: broadly lower matching -> divergent pollen and floral responses; Campanula historical calibration shows later autonomous-assurance transition

autonomous_reproductive_assurance.evidence: Campanula autonomous assurance is retained as a second-transition step in the historical calibration.
autonomous_reproductive_assurance.interpretation: Assurance is a plausible late propagation filter, but the current direct dependency field bundle is still missing.

physical_access_or_functional_matching.evidence: Corrected trait matching is lower across all eight shared targets.
physical_access_or_functional_matching.interpretation: A common-ish upstream mismatch signal is present but does not determine one downstream sign.

partner_effectiveness_or_service_redunda.interpretation: Matching-to-pollen propagation is positive but cluster-uncertain and network-state-sensitive; direct current effective-service calibration is incomplete.

resource_compensation.interpretation: No common source-locked resource-compensation axis explains the cross-taxon branching.

colonization_or_establishment_filtering.interpretation: Survivorship/non-establishment remains a programme response mode but is not the identified cause of the current eight-target sign branching.

network_rewiring_or_context.interpretation: Network-state sensitivity is observed downstream of matching and is a strong candidate branch allocator.

direct_reproductive_dependency.interpretation: Issue #91 is implementation-ready but real linked Campanula field rows are missing; this is the highest-value direct anchor measurement.

cross_case_discriminations.reason: Nicotiana supports high autonomous assurance as a buffer/establishment candidate, but Guaiacum shows a buffered exposure-to-breeding-index contrast despite negligible autogamy and vector-required reproduction. Hawaii remains unmeasured.

Ogasawara supplies a bounded access-to-fruit propagation case, whereas Hawaii shows signed mismatch and interaction-quality change with high reproductive performance and Izu shows downstream sign branching.
Hawaii buffers interaction-quality/resource changes before final reproduction and ABM v10 changes branch identity without broadening total branching.
Nicotiana island trait/selfing differences occur without a detected current island decrease in visitation or pollen transfer, leaving colonization/establishment filtering live.

The cases implicate different candidate filters: reproductive assurance in Nicotiana, possible resource compensation in Hawaii, unresolved partner/service compensation in Guaiacum, network-state allocation in Izu, and limited reproductive escape in propagating Ogasawara.

current_causal_reading.branch_generator: pre-existing functional/access position remains a viable branch-potential variable but is not a universal directional predictor
current_causal_reading.central_result: No single tested downstream filter explains all propagation states. The empirical programme now supports a multi-gate architecture in which the identity of the propagation filter is system-specific or unresolved.

ranked_next_measurements.measurement: same tagged population: effort + visitor/contact + SVD/no-visit controls + open/bagged-autonomous/supplemental-outcross + fruit/seed, with taxon-level FDQ traits where admissible
standardized per-visit pollen deposition/effectiveness by visitor and floral morph plus controlled exclusion/dependency; numeric access position only if source-native or newly measured prospectively
discriminates: low reproductive escape versus service asymmetry

ranked_next_measurements.measurement: controlled reproductive dependency/assurance in the same focal lobelioid populations and seasons as interaction-quality measurements
single-visit effectiveness and source-native numeric open/outcross dependency in the same observation/breeding trees if lawful source data exist
discriminates: Apis abundance compensation versus visitor diversity
stable breeding system versus stable total dependency

claim_boundary: This discriminator compares source-supported candidate mechanisms; it does not estimate causal effect sizes or assign a hidden cause where a source did not measure it. Candidate labels such as resource compensation or establishment filtering remain hypotheses unless the source directly discriminates them.
